title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Fri Sep 25, 2026
summary: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones overnight into September 24, killing 2 and injuring 8 and damaging a maternity hospital and a historic 1906 church, then hit the capital again overnight into September 25 with a mass drone barrage killing 7 — including two children — and injuring 59 across six districts plus Brovary and Lutsk. Ukraine responded on September 25 with long-range drone strikes on the Lukoil refinery in Perm (~1,450km inside Russia, 1 killed), the Iskra defense-electronics plant in Ulyanovsk (8 injured) and the Voronezhsintezkauchuk rubber/propellant plant in Voronezh (13 injured). Russian drones separately struck a medical center and ambulances in Zaporizhzhia, injuring 1. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,525,570 by September 25 per the Ukrainian General Staff.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Wed Sep 23, 2026
summary: Hours after Zelenskyy and Trump discussed an energy ceasefire at the UN on September 22, Russian drones pounded Kyiv on September 23, hitting petrol stations, the historic Shayba market and rail infrastructure, killing 2 and injuring 40+; separately, Russian aerial bombs killed 5 in Oleksandrivka, Donetsk Oblast. Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt energy strikes, but Kyiv said it was not informed of any deal. On September 22, a nationwide Russian missile and drone barrage killed 8 and wounded 37 across seven oblasts, including a strike on the Interpipe plant in Dnipro, while Ukrainian drones struck the Samara and Ufa oil refineries deep inside Russia.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Tue Sep 22, 2026

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Mon Sep 21, 2026
summary: Ukraine carried out its largest-ever drone/missile attack on a Moscow Oblast oil refinery and logistics facility overnight Sept 19-20, on the final day of Russia's Duma elections, killing 3 and injuring 20. The same day, Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps liberated Shandryholove and Derylove and took full control of Drobysheve in Operation Vivaldi's second phase in Donetsk Oblast. Russian drone strikes killed a mother and two children in Kyiv Oblast's Fastiv district and, separately, a woman near an apartment building in Sumy. The UN documented 1,004 verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence since 2022 (89% attributed to Russia), and the US State Department approved a $2.7 billion air-defense sale to Ukraine.
